About the Project Title: Advanced Web Design of Web Services
About Description: ErasmusHub was developed as part of the advanced web development and web services curriculum. It demonstrates a complete full-stack web application linking an accessible user interface, modern server-side PHP logic via Laravel, a relational MySQL database, a custom RESTful API (JSON/XML support), and external web service integrations (Open-Meteo weather service).
Feature 1 Description: Bilingual/trilingual frontend available in English, Portuguese, and Croatian, with responsive design, keyword search, category filtering, and live weather widgets.
Feature 2 Description: Complete publication lifecycle for articles and guides with draft and published states, image management, author attribution, and rich text editing.
Feature 3 Description: Strict authorization distinguishing Visitors, Registered Users, Editors, and Administrators, with instant session termination upon user deactivation.
Feature 4 Description: Fully documented RESTful API with standard HTTP response codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500), input validation, and pagination.
Feature 5 Description: Live weather information pulled from Open-Meteo with caching, custom timeout handling, and resilient error recovery.
Seminar Topic: Seminar Topic: The Evolution of Web Development
Seminar Description: Exploring the historical progression from static HTML/CGI pages to modern full-stack frameworks, reactive client-server architectures, and interconnected microservices and APIs.
